## Source-first maintenance loop

**INSPECT → VALIDATE → DETECT → CORRECT → REVIEW → VERIFY → USE**

Inspection is permitted while use is blocked. Repair the source under authorization,
then re-audit its affected consumers; do not create an overlapping replacement or
new dependency on an unreliable definition. Keep reviewed/corrected/uncertain status
separate from runtime approval.

## Portable execution and evidence

Tool names in legacy skill prose describe capabilities, not guaranteed host APIs.
Use the actual installed tool schema. `AskUserQuestion` means the available question
capability or a plain-text question; `Task` means an available, audited delegation
capability. Never invent a call, imply a subagent ran, or bypass an unavailable tool.
Unknown SKILL.md metadata is not permission enforcement or automatic command execution.

Resolve repository paths, source locale, build pipeline, standards and acceptance
criteria from the actual project before applying a template. Listed paths, example
metrics, capacity buffers and platform checklists are starting points, not evidence
that the project uses them. Do not impose optional dependencies or infrastructure.
Counts are not coverage, effort, completed behavior or readiness. Report unknowns,
zero/absent denominators and missing measurements explicitly; do not fill a template
with invented facts, owners, approvals, test results or performance gains.

Reuse answers and approval already given for the same scoped operation. Collaborative
questions capture missing material decisions, not repeated consent for an authorized
edit. Provide concise evidence and options, not a mandatory full analysis transcript.
Suggestions do not authorize subsequent features. Only one writer may mutate shared
files; parallel work must be isolated read-only analysis/tests with separate resources.

A team or producer recommendation is not deployment authorization. Report READY only for the exact tested artifact, environment and applicable criteria; required missing checks are BLOCKED. Deployment and monitoring require explicit scope and real configured tooling/owners. Do not promise background monitoring or treat an agent role as a human sign-off.

Apply only the requested polish scope and verified performance/accessibility targets. Examples such as camera shake or ambient effects are not authorization to add new features. Readiness concerns the reviewed feature/build, not the entire game by inference.

Respect established narrative intent, including deliberately unresolved mysteries. Do not invent canon or force a true answer where none is defined. Dialogue limits come from the actual presentation/localization constraints, not a universal character count.

Validate only the actual supported input/platform targets, including touch where relevant. Do not impose gamepad support on a touch-only product. Keep authoritative business state in its existing owner; local presentation state may remain in UI.

## Evidence and Metric Interpretation

Each percentage needs a defined denominator and an actual evidence source/revision.
With absent measurements or incomplete inventory, report UNKNOWN; a zero denominator
is N/A. Source/test-file counts do not establish implemented completeness or coverage.
Stage labels are diagnostic and do not certify a passed phase gate. Listed directory
paths are examples; map them to the inspected repository instead of assuming layout.

## Optional design-preview bounds

`pre-compact.sh` uses the existing `hook-checks.py` reader for both the checkpoint
and design WIP preview. Design text is UTF-8, regular, unlinked and at most 1 MiB
per file; the scan caps directory entries (4096), Markdown files (256), total input
(8 MiB), rendered matching lines (100) and excerpt output (32 KiB plus a summary).
Long matching lines are explicitly excerpted. Unsafe text, controls, special files,
unreadable data or exceeded input limits block before preview/logging rather than
claiming a clean scan. No markers is not design completeness or secret redaction.
The filesystem can still change between checks; this is not a hostile-filesystem
sandbox. Other Git/status output is not covered by the design-preview output cap.
